newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour renews attack on utility directors.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour renews attack on utility directors.

text.p: The opposition Labour party launched a twin attack on Monday on Britain's privatised utilities and the ruling Conservative party's declared goal of abolishing capital gains tax (CGT).
Labour said it had calculated that the directors of 21 water, power and telephone companies could be spared tax of more than 31 million pounds if CGT was scrapped.

Exposing what it called new executive excesses in the privatised utilities, Labour said figures compiled from company reports showed the directors had amassed potential profits from share options of more than 77 million pounds.

Economics spokesman Alan Milburn called on Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke in his annual budget on November 26 to drop plans to abolish CGT, which he said would benefit only a few, in favour of a 15 percent starting rate of income tax, which would help the many.
"Not only have the Tories failed to stamp out boardroom excess in the privatised utilties, their plan to axe CGT will hand their directors new risk-free fortunes," Milburn said.
"The Conservative party is acting more and more like the political arm of the privatised utilities," he added in a statement.

Labour's broadside comes in advance of a parliamentary debate it has called for Thursday on its plans for a windfall tax on the utilities' past profits to pay for measures to reduce long-term and youth unemployment.
